description: Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU), NSF NHERI 2025: Forces of Waterborne Debris on Elevated Coastal Structures is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Catrina Morin, Case Western Reserve University (case.edu). This project quantifies debris force data to understand its impact on elevated coastal structures. The analysis from this experiment can be reused to isolate different types of forces acting on the structure, allowing for further analysis of a specific type and using that as a basis for future experiments. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 3 top-level files (PDF). Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-gqpj-8s22. Keywords: Oregon State University O.H. Hinsdale Wave Research Laboratory, Debris, Waterborne Debris, Elevated Structures, Coastal Engineering, Wave Flume. Published 2025-09-19. Facility named: Large Wave Flume and Directional Wave Basin - Oregon State University. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
